misconception.description: taking a plain average of the contribution margins instead of weighting them by the sales mix, which misstates what an average sale contributes

worked_example.text: A kiosk sells drinks at a margin of EUR 1 and sandwiches at a margin of EUR 4, and sells three drinks for every sandwich. Its fixed costs are EUR 14,000 a month.
worked_example.solution: Weighted average margin = (3 x 1 + 1 x 4) / 4 = 7 / 4 = EUR 1.75 per item. Break-even = 14,000 / 1.75 = 8,000 items a month.

problem.text: A bakery sells two products. A loaf sells for EUR 8 with a variable cost of EUR 5; a cake sells for EUR 26 with a variable cost of EUR 17. The bakery sells two loaves for every cake, and its fixed costs are EUR 90,000 a year. How many items in total must it sell to break even?

distractors.note: the documented misconception: a plain average of the margins, as though loaves and cakes sold in equal numbers
using the loaf margin alone, as if the bakery sold nothing else

hints: There is no single margin here, so build one that reflects what the bakery actually sells: two loaves for every cake.
The margins are EUR 3 on a loaf and EUR 9 on a cake. In every group of three items sold, two are loaves and one is a cake, so weight them that way.
Divide the fixed costs by the weighted average margin to get the total number of items.
worked_solution: Step 1: the margins are 8 - 5 = EUR 3 on a loaf and 26 - 17 = EUR 9 on a cake. Step 2: weight by the mix. In every three items, two are loaves and one is a cake, so the average item contributes (2 x 3 + 1 x 9) / 3 = 15 / 3 = EUR 5. Step 3: divide: 90,000 / 5 = 18,000 items a year, which is 12,000 loaves and 6,000 cakes. A plain average of EUR 3 and EUR 9 would give EUR 6 and 15,000 items, understating what the bakery has to sell because it assumes as many cakes as loaves.

near_transfer.text: The same bakery, selling two loaves for every cake and breaking even at 18,000 items in total, wants the split. How many cakes must it sell?

distractors.note: splitting the total evenly, ignoring the two-to-one mix
reporting the loaves instead of the cakes

far_transfer.text: The same bakery sells loaves at EUR 8 and cakes at EUR 26, two loaves for every cake. What is the weighted average selling price of an item?

distractors.note: a plain average, ignoring that twice as many loaves are sold
the weights attached to the wrong products
